answer: A harbor office enrolls one ledger key per human after staff check a government ID and fingerprint; the registry rejects duplicate biometric templates, so extra identities need separate humans, not extra keys. A serial-numbered ferrous token is checked against that biometric, not accepted alone. Renewal after a fixed horizon repeats the duplicate check. Attacker gain is n(R-C), deterring only while R<C; bribable staff, forged IDs and matcher errors remain risks.
